recommendation: Keep the no-change audit commit as-is. No follow-up is needed for FHIR-14831 unless a future work group decision explicitly asks for additional search parameter aliases or a different naming policy.
issue_request: FHIR-14831 was a Published/Persuasive FHIR-core Medication request from the Pharmacy work group, raised for STU3, asking for search based on medication batch number and expiry date. The accepted resolution was to add lotnumber and expirationDate as two new Medication search parameters.
initial_application: The Jira application comment cites fhir-svn commit 73c779d3aeb5a6120955eb499d67727c2fdfdf47. That commit explicitly mentions TR# 14831 and added the lower-case dash-delimited search rows lot-number and expiration-date on Medication.batch.lotNumber and Medication.batch.expirationDate.
additional_context: Medication remains an active resource in source/fhir.ini. The current resource model uses Medication.instance for the former batch backbone, with fhir.ini compatibility mappings from Medication.batch.expirationDate and Medication.batch.lotNumber to Medication.instance.expirationDate and Medication.instance.lotNumber. The current Medication search-parameter bundle contains Medication-expiration-date with code expiration-date, type date, and expression Medication.instance.expirationDate, plus Medication-lot-number with code lot-number, type token, and expression Medication.instance.lotNumber. The underlying Medication structure definition still defines both instance fields. Zulip and Confluence searches found no relevant contrary discussion.
reconciliation: No source change was made. An empty audit commit was published because the current build-scope source already carries the two requested search parameters using the original dash-delimited search names and the current Medication.instance element paths.

related_jiras.note: The same historical SVN commit also added Medication serial-number material, but that is a separate request and was not needed to decide FHIR-14831.
